headline: High-risk shared-workspace coding agent can overwrite or mislead Prefect workflows; prompt-injection and compliance risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, use MCP, and run browsers; Prefect is an orchestration/data-engineering system that can consume workflow metadata. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge could let attacker-controlled content in Cline’s workspace influence Prefect inputs. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Cline writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that Prefect later parses
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes Cline output into Prefect without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP/file bridges between agents for untrusted content
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes any Cline-generated file
Use allowlisted file paths only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots, writes the filesystem, and has broad network egress; Prefect also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive code or screenshots can flow from Cline into Prefect outputs or remote calls. The profiles do not show local-only inference or isolation, so leakage is plausible in default workspace-sharing setups.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same workspace directory
IF Cline stores screenshots or code in files that Prefect uploads or logs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Restrict Prefect to metadata-only inputs
Turn off automatic uploads/logging for shared artifacts
Rotate or redact screenshots before saving
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, with shared state via filesystem; Prefect can also act on files and remote APIs. Concurrent writes to the same workspace or git repo can corrupt state or overwrite each other, and no locking is documented. This is dangerous by default when both operate in the same repo.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same git repository or workspace directory
IF no external lock or serialization is enforced
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories
Serialize write operations with a manual lock
Pause one agent while the other commits
Review diffs before any commit or deploy
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, or files that Prefect may treat as workflow metadata or inputs. If Prefect consumes those outputs without verification, errors can cascade into automated orchestration actions. The pair does not document a verification boundary, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Cline-produced files as authoritative workflow inputs
IF no validation step checks Cline outputs before orchestration
mitigations: Require schema validation on all Cline-produced artifacts
Add a human approval gate before Prefect runs downstream tasks
Compare outputs against a second source
Log and diff inputs before execution
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code, browser screenshots, and model-provider API keys, while Prefect is documented here only as touching workflow metadata. No explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is shown, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive code or screenshots in shared workflows. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline’s workspace and then propagated into Prefect logs or metadata
IF screenshots or secrets are stored in shared artifacts
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from shared workflows
Redact secrets before saving files
Review retention settings on Prefect logs
Use separate storage for screenshots and code
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
